sources.title: Nasdaq-100 index methodology, copyright 2026
sources.excerpt: The Nasdaq-100 Index is designed to measure the performance of 100 of the largest Nasdaq-listed non-financial companies. The Index employs a modified market capitalization weighting scheme. Multiple classes of securities issued by the same company are each eligible, subject to meeting all other Security Eligibility Criteria. A company must not be classified in the Financial Industry under the Industry Classification Benchmark (ICB). REITs are not eligible. For the purpose of weight calculations, Modified Market Capitalization will be utilized. Only the market capitalization of eligible listed share classes will be considered. Foreign-listed and unlisted shares are disregarded. Each low-float security's Total Shares Outstanding (TSO) will be capped at three times the number of its free-floating shares. A Fast Entry inclusion will not require the removal of another security, and may temporarily increase the constituent count to more than 100. Reconstitution Frequency Annually; Rebalance Frequency Quarterly.

sources.title: Holdings & Sector Allocations of Invesco QQQ
sources.excerpt: Invesco QQQ ETF tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index — giving you access to the performance of the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq. The fund and the index are rebalanced quarterly and reconstituted annually. The Fund is non-diversified and may experience greater volatility than a more diversified investment. Shares are not individually redeemable and owners of the Shares may acquire those Shares from the Funds and tender those shares for redemption to the Funds in Creation Unit aggregations only, typically consisting of 50,000 Shares.

price.note: Regular-session close, not NAV or after-hours. Observed current fund-unit basis; no ADR conversion.

shares.note: Actual fund units outstanding, not EPS weighted average. Second precisely dated independent observation not available.

market_cap.note: ETF net assets/AUM are net portfolio value, not reported corporate equity market capitalization. No comparable dated reported quoted-unit capitalization retained; native price times units remains only an arithmetic product.

revenue.note: Investment income and portfolio turnover are not corporate customer revenue; fund mandate is index exposure.

net_income.note: Fund net investment income and realized/unrealized gains are investment-company results, not consolidated operating-company GAAP net income.

operating_cash_flow.note: Creations/redemptions and portfolio security cash flows do not measure operating-company cash generation.

capital_expenditure.note: Fund portfolio purchases are investments, not cash PP&E capital spending; no operating-company capex applies.

cash.note: Any fund cash/collateral is a portfolio allocation/settlement item, not consolidated corporate liquidity available for capital allocation.

debt.note: Underlying bond holdings (especially TLT Treasuries) are fund assets, not the fund operating-company debt; settlement liabilities are not a comparable corporate capital structure.

eps.note: No corporate GAAP diluted EPS earning-capacity anchor for an index fund; distributions and NAV changes are not operating EPS.

fund_nav.note: Sponsor net asset value per fund unit; not executable market price.
